newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods flat as players sidElined.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods flat as players sidElined.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices remained unchanged in idle Thursday trade, with players out of the market to assess how far the NYMEX product and crude market would drop, trade sources said.
"There's been nothing going on," one broker said.
NYMEX March unleaded gasoline dipped 1.90 cents a gallon to 62.78 cents, weighed by lower crude futures, which fell on the last trading day of March contracts.
A 1.55-cent slide in heating oil futures also weighed on West Coast spot trade, while NYMEX crude sank 81 cents a barrel.

Offers for conventional unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles were 68 cents a gallon, flat from Wedneday. Sellers priced CARB-grade gasoline at 74 cents, unchanged in a market where no deals were heard done Thursday.
Bay area gasoline stood around three cents a gallon lower than L.A. material.
Distillates were also flat, with low sulphur diesel offers at 71 cents.
